name: The Dead Card Reader
setup: Owen's Level B2 keycard swipes and the panel only flashes orange. The reader has lost its conduit plug in the grey wall box left of the bulkhead frame; seat the plug, then swipe, then survive a ten-second reset beep that draws two Husks down the corridor.
solution: Open the grey wall box and push the loose conduit plug home (two interacts, a click each), then swipe KEY_C3_KeycardB2 at the reader and hold the corridor for the 10 s reset. The bulkhead cycles open.
failure: No hard fail. Swiping with the plug loose only chirps the panel and makes a small noise ping. Being grabbed during the reset cancels it and it must be redone; running during the reset leaves two roused Husks loose in the lab corridor.
hint_1: The card's good, I watched it light the panel orange. So it isn't the card.
hint_2: There's a snag list back in the labs that moans about this exact reader. Grey wall box, left of the frame.
hint_3: Open the box, push the loose plug in until it clicks twice, then swipe. And watch the corridor, the reset beeps for ages.
hint_trigger: hint_1 at 60 s idle or 1 failed swipe; hint_2 at 120 s or 3 failed swipes; hint_3 at 200 s or 4 failed swipes

name: The Security Office Keypad
setup: The B2 security office is a special room behind a four-digit keypad. The security chief, tired of being asked, wrote his hint on a sticky note stuck to the lab whiteboard frame, because the board is where staff stood around.
solution: The whiteboard header reads TRIAL 07 / RUN 03. The sticky note says trial number then run number, two digits each. Enter 0703 on the keypad to open the security office, which holds KEY_C3_MasterKey and the shipment clearance countersigned by W. Hale.
failure: Three wrong codes trip a tamper buzzer: a 15 s red-screen lockout and a loud noise event that pulls the security wing's patrolling Brute to the door. The code never changes and attempts are never capped.
hint_1: Four digits and a note from a man who thought he was being funny. It's on the board.
hint_2: Read the top line of the whiteboard, not the table. Trial number, then run number.
hint_3: Trial seven, run three. Two digits each. Zero seven, zero three.
hint_trigger: hint_1 at 45 s at the keypad or 1 wrong entry; hint_2 at 120 s or 2 wrong entries; hint_3 at 240 s or 4 wrong entries

name: Flooding the Cooling Chamber
setup: The cold vault is behind an interlock that only releases once the neighbouring cooling chamber has been taken through a complete V-7 cold-shock ladder. Three hand valves on the gallery: 1 BRINE INTAKE (floods to +4 C), 2 CRYO (takes a flooded chamber to -12 C, dead on a dry chamber), 3 PURGE (dumps the chamber and ends the run). A gauge shows chamber temperature with a green HOLD lamp that lights at the stage temperature and goes dark when the hold is served. Two Drowned lie in the chamber sump and are killed by the cryo stage.
solution: Run the four-stage cold-shock ladder in order, serving every hold: stage 1 Valve 1 INTAKE to +4 C, hold 90 s; stage 2 Valve 2 CRYO to -12 C, hold 30 s; stage 3 close CRYO and reopen Valve 1 INTAKE back to +4 C, hold 60 s; stage 4 Valve 3 PURGE. In-game hold times play at quarter speed (about 22 s / 8 s / 15 s). The interlock releases the cold vault. The identical ladder (4 C, -12 C, 4 C, purge) is what the Chapter 5 synthesis machine demands, gated on FLG_C3_ColdShockKnown.
failure: Purging before stage 4, opening CRYO on a dry chamber, or turning any valve before the HOLD lamp goes dark trips the relief vent: 4 s of live steam across the gallery (Caution-level contact damage and a screen whiteout), the gauge drops to ambient and the run resets to stage 1. Unlimited retries; each failed run spawns one extra Drowned up the gallery stair.
hint_1: The vault's holding its own door shut. It wants the chamber run properly first.
hint_2: That log you copied down. Four stages, plus four, minus twelve, plus four, purge. The gauge is the board, the valves are the pen.
hint_3: Intake until the lamp dies, cryo until it dies, shut cryo and intake again until it dies, then purge. Purge last or the vent blows.
hint_trigger: hint_1 on entering the gallery or 60 s idle; hint_2 on the first relief vent trip or 150 s; hint_3 on the second trip or 300 s

name: The Warden: Gas, Doors and a Fuel Line
setup: The coolant plant floor is four hazard-striped bays with three yellow gas valves and four droppable blast doors. The Warden's plate shrugs off pistol and rifle fire from the front; a weeping fuel line under his back plate is the only soft thing on him, and only a gas flash in a sealed bay can strip that plate.
solution: Open a bay's gas valve (6 s to fill), draw the Warden into that bay with noise or with yourself, then pull the bay lever so the blast door traps the gas with him. Fuel off his own pack ignites it on the hot pipe run, buckling his back plate and exposing the fuel line for 4 s. Shoot the line. Three exposures kill him; after the second he blocks one valve, so each cycle must use a different bay.
failure: Standing in a bay when it flashes is heavy damage and a knockdown, lethal from Danger health. Sealing an empty bay wastes its gas and costs 20 s of recharge. All three bays spent at once forces a dodging phase until a valve recharges. Death reloads at the arena entry with doors open and gas reset.
hint_1: Pistol's doing nothing to that plate. Use the room.
hint_2: Yellow gas valves on the bay walls. Open one, get him standing in it, then drop the blast door on the bay.
hint_3: The blast strips his back plate. There's a fuel line under it. Shoot the line while it's bare, you've got about four seconds.
hint_trigger: hint_1 after 25 s of front-plate fire with no weak-point hit; hint_2 at 60 s or after the first wasted bay; hint_3 at 100 s or the first missed 4 s window

name: The Undertow Raft Fight
setup: A spline set-piece through a field of rock pillars to the cave mouth. Mara rows and steers, Leon kneels at the bow with rifle and flare gun. The player's two verbs are calling the turn (left or right, which is the steering input routed through Mara's rowing stroke) and shooting the eye when the hooded ridge opens.
solution: Phase 1: call left or right to clear alternating pillar pairs and shoot the eye in the 3 s it surfaces before each tentacle swing, which cancels the swing. Phase 2: it grips the gunwale and the eye closes; put five rifle rounds or one flare into the coiled arm to break the grip while Mara bails. Phase 3: it rises across the cave mouth with the eye wide; sustained fire into the open eye over a 12 s window, a flare counting for four rifle rounds, and it sinks under the raft as the current carries them out.
failure: A missed pillar call costs a third of the hull; hull at zero in phase 1 or 2, or too little damage in phase 3, capsizes the raft, with a short drowning cut and a reload to the phase start. Checkpoints at each phase start, and ammunition is topped up at each checkpoint so the player is never dry in a fight they cannot leave.
hint_1: I can't steer and watch. Call it or we're on the rocks.
hint_2: It opens that eye before it swings. That's your window, not after.
hint_3: If it's got hold of the raft, shoot the arm, not the eye. Free us first.
hint_trigger: hint_1 after 2 missed pillar calls; hint_2 after 3 eye surfacings with no hit; hint_3 at 8 s into phase 2 with the arm untouched
